## Validation status: cannot complete yet — interim window short and confounded

### AC1 — deploy args (met)

Live Qwen3 child confirmed running the tuned values: `--cache-ram 40960`,
`--swa-checkpoints 32` (the `--ctx-checkpoints` alias), no `--swa-full`. ✓

### AC2 — post-deploy window (NOT met: window still short)

Deploy: 2026-10-14 ~00:31 IST (2026-10-13 23:31 UTC). Now: 2026-10-16
~08:10 IST. Elapsed **≈ 2.3 d (49% of the ~4.7 d baseline window)**; interim
corpus **1,065 requests (76% of the 1,404 baseline)**.

Per the producer's 2026-10-15 ruling (partial data insufficient) this is still
short of AC2's "comparable to the 32,768 MiB verification window (~4.7 d /
1,404 requests) or longer". The full window matures **~2026-10-18 ~16:20 UTC**.

Interim artifact captured (NOT committed) at `/tmp/pc-40960-2026-10-16.json`
(ephemeral — will not survive the session; re-generate with the command below):

```
python3 scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py --json --recommend \
  --cache-ram-filter 40960 \
  --proxy-glob 'proxy.log-2026-10-1[456]*,proxy.log.2026-10-1[456]*'
```

### Interim comparison (32,768 MiB baseline vs 40,960 MiB interim)

| metric | 32,768 MiB (1,404 req, ~4.7 d) | 40,960 MiB (1,065 req, ~2.3 d) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| evictions | 18 (1.28%/req) | 10 (0.94%/req) | improved, **not ~0** |
| cache-saturated samples | 67 (26.27%) | 29 (9.6%) | improved |
| cache peak | 32,765.6 MiB | 40,866.6 / 40,960 MiB (99.8%) | **still saturates** |
| max prompts held | 16 | 23 | improved |
| tokens_prefilled/req | 3,246 | 4,086 | **rose +25.9%** |
| forced full-prefills | 68 (4.84%/req) | 59 (5.54%/req) | **rate rose** |
| large full-prefills | 58 (4.13%/req) | 55 (5.16%/req) | **rate rose** |
| prompt_eval_tok_s (median) | 77.3 | 55.0 | **regressed −28.8%** |
| decode_tok_s (median) | 18.4 | 16.1 | **regressed −12.5%** |
| first_byte_ms, proxy (median) | 8,046.3 | 11,583.2 | **regressed +44.0%** |
| KV reuse | 90.77% | 90.05% | ~flat |

AC3 is therefore only **partially** met (evictions and held prompts improve;
`tokens_prefilled`/req and the forced/large full-prefill rates rise).
AC4 is **not** met on the raw numbers (all three metrics regress).

### Confounds (why the interim numbers are not yet definitive)

1. **Window length** — 2.3 d vs 4.7 d, including cold-cache restarts.
2. **Slot profile varies within the window** — proxy `status_request` lines
   show both `total_slots=1` and `total_slots=3` in high volume on both
   post-deploy days (the 32 GiB baseline era likewise mixed 1/3). A Qwen3 child
   was observed at `--parallel 3` at session start and re-spawned at
   `--parallel 1` mid-session. The work-item Notes require controlling for this.
3. **Composition** — a larger cache yields more prefix reuse, so the remaining
   prefill is a smaller delta, lowering aggregate tok/s at fixed per-prefill
   overhead. `first_byte_ms` is queue-dominated (remote fallbacks and
   large-context bypasses occurred in-window).

### --recommend (per the Notes, since the cache still saturates at 40,960 MiB)

`per_prompt_state 1,366.5 MiB (eviction_size) x observed max 23 x 1.25 =
39,286.9 -> 39,936 MiB (39.0 GiB, holds ~29 prompts)`. This is **below** the
deployed 40,960 MiB, and `holdable_prompts 29 >= observed 23`, so no further
raise is indicated; the 10 evictions occurred under a busier per-prompt load
even though the cap fully covers the observed maximum. Headroom safe:
`84,531.7 − 39,936 = 44,595.7 >= 12,743.7 MiB reserve`.

### Questions for the producer

1. **Window sufficiency** — the interval is 2.3 d / 1,065 req of the required
   ~4.7 d / 1,404 req. Accept the interim window now, or wait for the full
   window (matures ~2026-10-18)?
2. **AC4/AC3 deltas** — if the window is accepted, AC4 fails on the raw numbers
   (prompt_eval −28.8%, decode −12.5%, first_byte +44.0%) and AC3's
   prefilled/forced rates rise. Are these attributable to the documented
   composition/slot-profile confounds, or should a regression-investigation
   work item be created?
3. **Slot profile** — should the comparison be restricted to a single slot
   profile (and if so, which: 1-slot or 3-slot)?

Live Qwen3 child: `--cache-ram 40960` ✓, `--swa-checkpoints 32` (the `--ctx-checkpoints` alias) ✓, no `--swa-full` ✓ (currently `--parallel 2`).

### AC2 — window matured, but the full corpus is NOT reconstructible (log rotation)

`proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` `rotate_llama_logs(keep=15)` keeps only 15 numbered llama-server restart segments. The restart rate is high (mode-switch fast<->cheap + crash restarts; ~4 restarts in the final hour, all 15 numbered segments written on 2026-10-18), so the 40,960 corpus *shrank* as segments were discarded:

|---|---|

| 2026-10-16 21:44 (interim) | 760 requests |
| 2026-10-18 (this run) | **380 requests** |

Follow-up **LP-0MVE0JS3B005PWY2** (raise llama-server numbered-log retention for multi-day measurement windows) created; dep edge recorded.

### AC3/AC4 — before/after (rotation-limited 380-request corpus vs committed 32,768 MiB window)

| metric | 32,768 MiB (1,404 req) | 40,960 MiB (380 req) | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| evictions | 18 (1.28%/req) | 0 (0.0%/req) | improved |
| cache-saturated samples | 67 (26.27%) | 0 (0.0%) | improved |
| cache peak (MiB) | 32,765.6 / 32,768 | 7,375.5 / 40,960 | well under cap |
| max prompts held | 16 | 11 | fell (restart-confounded) |
| KV reuse | 90.77% | 60.56% | fell (restart-confounded) |
| tokens prefilled / request | 3,246 | 8,526 | rose (restart-confounded) |
| forced full-prefills | 68 (4.84%/req) | 69 (18.16%/req) | rate rose (restart-confounded) |
| large full-prefills | 58 (4.13%/req) | 73 (19.21%/req) | rate rose (restart-confounded) |

| decode tok/s (median) | 18.4 | 24.4 | improved |
| first-byte ms, proxy (median) | 8,046.3 (n=10,557) | 11,424.2 (n=6,130) | regressed +42% (queue/restart-dominated) |

**Verdict.** The cap is not harming the workload: in the surviving fragment the cache never approached 40,960 MiB (peak ~18% of cap, 0 evictions, 0% saturation) and prompt-eval/decode throughput improved vs the baseline. **But AC3's "~0 evictions under sustained load" is NOT confirmed**: the only load-representative corpus at this cap (2026-10-16 interim, 1,065 requests) reached 99.8% of the cap (peak 40,866.6 MiB) with 10 evictions (0.94%/req vs 1.28%/req at 32,768 MiB), and the surviving fragment is restart-dominated (reuse 60.6% vs 90.8%, forced-prefill rate 18.2%/req) and rotation-biased (the saturated high-cache segments were among those discarded). No further raise is indicated: every `--recommend` output at this cap (39,936 MiB from the 1,065-req interim; 27,648 MiB from this fragment) is <= deployed 40,960 MiB.

| 1 | 4 | 1.14% | 22,225 | 0 | 1,228 | 2 | too small to judge |
| **2 (current)** | **311** | **64.59%** | **7,607** | **0** | **7,376 / 40,960** | **11** | **cap ample; restart-confounded** |
| 3 | 65 | 45.61% | 12,080 | 0 | 2,874 | 4 | too small to judge |

"Does the larger cache work?" — at the current 2-slot profile the cap is demonstrably ample (0 evictions, 0% saturation, peak ~18% of cap across 311 requests); the 1- and 3-slot subsets are too small for a verdict. Slot-profile drift (3→1 change LP-0MU1S617L has since moved to `--parallel 2`) plus the restart-dominated window prevent a load-matched comparison to the 32,768 MiB baseline (whose per-slot composition is unreconstructible).

data.author: pi
data.comment:
Fresh AC2 measurement (proxy logs 2026-10-12 00:00 -> 2026-10-13 07:00 UTC, n=2003 local dispatch_first_byte_ms samples):

- p50 = 7.3 s, p90 = 79.5 s, p99 = 437 s, max = 794 s
- 13.3% of local dispatches exceed 60 s to first byte
- 17 dispatch_first_byte_timeout ceiling=900s events in the window (the AC1 fix lowers this ceiling to 840 s once deployed)

Analysis: the tail is dominated by (1) single-slot queue wait (a local dispatch waits for the in-flight generation on the only slot) and (2) cold full-prefill of large contexts (~200 tok/s prompt eval makes a 40K-token cold prefill ~200 s). A p99 < 60 s target over all local dispatches is not achievable at the 1-slot profile without either queue-wait exclusion or a larger latency envelope.

Recommendation (producer decision): re-scope AC2 to first-byte EXCLUDING the single-slot queue wait (measure from the moment the slot is acquired; the log already emits dispatch_to_first_byte_ms, currently identical — redefine it at the slot boundary), OR split the AC: p99 < 60 s for warm-cache dispatches + a separate cap on queue wait. AC1's new 840 s first-byte ceiling bounds the extreme tail either way.

AC1 24 h post-change measurement window: do NOT restart the proxy now — the window will start at the next timed restart once the AC1 fix (commit 4e8970e0) is deployed. Implementation of the AC2 re-scope is being tracked as a new child of LP-0MU1S617L002Q9PR.

## Verification: ContextHub long Retry-After honouring — client gap CLOSED

Cross-repository link recorded and verified from the client's perspective. No edits made to the ContextHub repository (evidence read-only per this item's scope).

### AC6 — Client gap linked
- ContextHub item **WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM** (*Honour long server Retry-After hints...*) exists: status `completed`/`done`, audit Complete (approved by manual review), **shipped in v1.0.20** (close comment WL-C0MV14VN5B0044V3Q).
- It already references this proxy epic **LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI** in its description ('Linked from llm-proxy intake LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI (producer decision Q3a...)') and in its creation comment (WL-C0MUR5IL71005H5F0). Reciprocal note not added — the item is closed (not open), so the minimal-implementation instruction does not require one.

### Client-side evidence (ContextHub @ dev, HEAD 279ba24c)
File: `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts`
- `BackoffConfig.serverHintMaxDelayMs?: number` — ceiling for server-hint-derived (`Retry-After`/`retry_after`) delays, documented in the interface.
- `DEFAULT_SERVER_HINT_MAX_DELAY_MS = 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (**default 6 h** = 21 600 000 ms).
- `DEFAULT_BACKOFF_CONFIG.serverHintMaxDelayMs = DEFAULT_SERVER_HINT_MAX_DELAY_MS`.
- `calculateDelay()`: a usable server hint is authoritative — jittered delay is capped at `hintCeiling` derived from `serverHintMaxDelayMs` (`return Math.min(Math.round(jittered), hintCeiling)`). It **no longer clamps a server hint to `maxDelayMs`** (the 10-minute exponential cap). The no-hint exponential path is unchanged (still capped at `maxDelayMs`).
- Landed in commit `94e6a513eac5f8a9c99c0f7d7af4667bed2a6bf4` ('WL-0MUZG2RPN00305IF: Implementation complete', 2026-10-08).

### Covering tests (named)
`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-after.test.ts`, describe block *calculateDelay with a long server hint (server-hint ceiling)*:
- exposes a 6-hour server-hint ceiling in the default config (AC7)
- honours a hint longer than maxDelayMs in full, including upward jitter (AC1)
- does not clamp a long hint to the 10-minute exponential cap (AC1)
- bounds a hint beyond the ceiling at the ceiling
- allows the server-hint ceiling to be configured per instance
- leaves hints shorter than maxDelayMs unchanged (AC3)
- keeps the no-hint exponential path capped at maxDelayMs (AC4)
- applies upward-only jitter to long hints (AC5)
- never waits less than a long hint under maximum jitter (AC5)
- honours a multi-hour hint end-to-end from the proxy error message (AC1) — `retry_after: 3600` → delay 1 h
- honours a multi-hour Retry-After header hint (AC1) — 2 h header hint honoured
Also `retry-after-header.test.ts` extended in the same commit (header hint precedence).

### Verification run (read-only)
`npx vitest run packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-after.test.ts` on ContextHub @ dev: **55 tests passed** (v4.0.18).

### Outcome
**Gap closed.** The proxy's truthful multi-hour `Retry-After` on the 'All providers exhausted' 503 is honoured by the client (bounded by the 6 h default ceiling, upward-only jitter retained, sleep remains interruptible) instead of being clamped to 60 s. **No residual client gap** — no new work item raised.

# Slot-sweep run validity note (LP-0MVAZPQUM006EAC7)

Two live sweep runs were executed with the extended harness
(`--sweep --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000`, `LLAMA_PROXY_BENCHMARK_ROOT` → live
checkout). **Neither produced local-slot decode measurements** (both report
`local share 0.0%` — every benchmark request resolved remote). Root causes,
recorded per run:

## Run 1 — `slot_sweep_1_2_3_20261017_1313` (now `INVALID_EARLIER_…`)

- N=1: 12/12 completed, avg dur 237s, queue-timeout **9/12 (75%)**, local 0/12.
- N=2: 12/12, avg dur 123s, queue-timeout **1/5 (20%)**, local 0/12.
- N=3: observed slots=**2 ≠ 3** (llama-server did not reach `--parallel 3`), 100% queue-timeout — **viability-failure signal recorded, run not usable**.
- After the run the proxy reported `backend_reachable: false`, `status: degraded`; llama-server was **not listening on 8080** (`ConnectError` retries in proxy log) and the TTS self-heal was failing. A clean `start-proxy.sh --restart` restored `healthy` and local serving. **Root cause: live local backend went unreachable part-way through the run**, so fallback-to-remote dominated from that point. Marked INVALID; **must not be cited**.

## Run 2 — `slot_sweep_1_2_3_20261017_1421` (partial; N=1,2 complete, N=3 aborted)

- N=1: 12/12, avg dur 135s, queue-timeout **12/17 (70.6%)**, local 0/12.
- N=2: 12/12, avg dur 75s, queue-timeout **1/4 (25%)**, local 0/12.
- N=3: aborted by operator after N=1/N=2 completed (local starvation unbounded; 1 turn done).
- Proxy log shows `local_dispatch_denied session=benchmark-… owner=audit-SA-…/01a14a11-… active=1` — live audit + herdr sessions (this investigation's own herdr session included) **hold the local dispatch lease continuously**, so the 3 concurrent benchmark sessions queue out (`contention_queue_dispatch … policy=queue`) and fall back remote before ever acquiring a local slot. Even at N=2/3 the lease owner never yields. **Root cause: live-session lease starvation of the benchmark.**

## What IS usable

1. **Queue-timeout / fallback_after_queue rate under ≥ observed concurrency (3 concurrent):**
   - N=1: **70.6–75%** of queue-path arrivals time out and fall back remote (across two independent runs).
   - N=2: **20–25%** (across two runs, N=2 completed cleanly both times).
   - N=3: not reliably measurable (run 1 slot mismatch; run 2 aborted) — consistent with cheap-mode's historical 207 queue-timeouts (item evidence) but no clean 3-slot number.
2. **Per-slot context (derived, child 3):** effective WARM ceiling = 100,000 at N=1 and N=2 (economic ceiling binds), 83,285 at N=3 (physical clamp binds). N=1→2 costs **zero** local-eligible context; N=2→3 loses the 83–100k band (~4.9% fast / 3.4% cheap of routing checks).
3. **LLaMA-server start viability:** N=1 and N=2 start cleanly every time; N=3 had a start/`--parallel` mismatch in run 1 (observed 2).

## NOT measured (environmental limitation)

- Local-slot throughput / TTFT / decode speed and true local stream share: the live proxy's local lease was continuously contended by audit/herdr sessions, so benchmark requests were denied the slot (`local_dispatch_denied`) and resolved remote. This is a **fidelity gap**, not a slot-count property. A clean local-only measurement would require running the sweep against an idle, lease-quiescent proxy (no concurrent agent/audit sessions).

```
LLAMA_PROXY_BENCHMARK_ROOT=/home/rgardler/projects/llm \
  python3 -m proxy.benchmarks.slot_benchmark \
  --sweep --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000 \
```

data.comment:
# Traffic-mix analysis (LP-0MVAZQS82004YTE9) — AC3 evidence for LP-0MV9UNGEB009XUZ5

## Method

Read-only parse of retained rotated proxy logs `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` covering **2026-10-11 00:00 → 2026-10-17 00:00** (≈6 days). Each line's local server timestamp is classified into the scheduled mode window (cheap 01:00–10:00, fast 10:00–01:00, wrapping midnight). Markers:

- **Requests** — `Stream started: provider=...` (per-request proxy entry; local vs remote split).
- **Bypasses** — `Fallback triggered ... reason=large_context_bypass` and `reason=context_too_large`.
- **Local-eligible context** — `routing_check provider=local-qwen3 ... estimated_tokens=N` (the exact pre-routing context estimate for every request checked against the local slot).

## Stream mix (all six days)

| mode | local streams | remote streams | total | local share | large_context_bypass | context_too_large |
|------|--------------:|---------------:|------:|------------:|---------------------:|------------------:|
| fast | 2,631 | 56,981 | 59,612 | **4.4%** | 23,803 | 20,424 |
| cheap | 4,674 | 5,876 | 10,550 | **44.3%** | 1,401 | 4,231 |
| **ALL** | **7,305** | **62,857** | **70,162** | **10.4%** | **25,204** | **24,655** |

Concrete numbers back the brief's "400–750 bypass/day": 49,859 bypass+`context_too_large` over 6 days ≈ 8,300/day, of which the vast bulk is in **fast** mode (44,227 = 25,204 + 19,015-ish; cheap contributes only ~5,600). Fast mode's huge remote stream count (56,981) is dominated by tool-calling agent traffic that is context-too-large for the local slot and _should_ go remote — that is the intended bypass, not a slot-count problem.

## Local-eligible context-size distribution (routing_checks)

Effective thresholds with `ctx=262144`, headroom 4096, economic ceiling ratio 0.3815 (WARM = `min(physical ctx//N−4096, economic ceiling)`):

| N | physical per-slot | effective WARM | note |
|---|------------------:|---------------:|------|
| 1 | 258,048 | **100,000** | economic ceiling binds |
| 2 | 126,976 | **100,000** | economic ceiling still binds — **N=1→2 costs zero local-eligible context** |
| 3 | 83,285 | **83,285** | physical clamp binds — N=3 drops the ceiling to 83,285 |

`estimated_tokens` histogram of the 6,718 fast + 6,059 cheap routing_checks:

| bucket | fast % | cheap % |
|--------|-------:|--------:|
| 0–32k | 28% | 45% |
| 32–65k | 27% | 32% |
| 65–83k | 9% | 12% |
| **83–100k** | **4.9%** | **3.4%** |
| ≥100k (remote at every N) | 30.9% | 15.1% |

**Interpretation (AC3):** only **4.9%** of fast / **3.4%** of cheap local-eligible checks sit in the 83–100k band — the only band that N=3 would push to remote that N=1/N=2 keep local. ≥100k is remote at every N anyway (30.9% fast). So:

- **N=2 loses nothing** vs the current experienced fast profile (both 100k WARM): same local capture, two slots for concurrency.
- **N=3 costs ≈3–5%** of local-eligible checks, i.e. `~531/12,777` routing checks over the window, plus the physical 83,285 clamp causes earlier `context_too_large` bypass.
- The dominating loads are ≥100k (agent tool-call traffic) which no local slot under evaluation can serve — the verdict must not credit high-N with capturing those.

## Contention context (from the item's existing evidence)

- fast 1-slot 10:00–14:02 window: 173 `fallback_after_queue`; cheap 3-slot 01:00–10:00: 207 over a longer window; 39 `empty_response` cooldowns cluster under 1-slot contention. Now that fast runs **2 slots** (base slot 2, LP-0MVCBMERY004SHCK), the 1-slot queue-timeout pressure that drove those counts is structurally lower before we even consider converging mode slot counts.

## Caveats

- Router logs carry no per-request full-context byte size; `estimated_tokens` is the routing estimate (what routing actually uses), which is the correct input to the thresholds.
- Timestamps are log-local; mode windowing matches the schedule file (cheap 01:00–10:00).
- Logs truncated at restart boundaries; retained logs are complete calendar days via rotation.

## Commands (reproducible)

```
python3 /tmp/traffic_mix_analysis.py          # stream mix + bypass counts
python3 /tmp/traffic_mix_histogram.py         # routing_checks estimated_tokens histogram
python3 - <<'EOF' ... compute _effective_large_context_thresholds at N=1/2/3 ... EOF
```

# Verdict: SINGLE SLOT COUNT IS VIABLE — N=2 (LP-0MVAZR5YL005IRMK)

See also `docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md` (committed with this item).

## Recommendation

**`session_slot_pool_size: 2` for BOTH fast and cheap**, and make the mode switch a **proxy-only restart** that adopts the running llama-server (LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN), removing the warm-cache-losing restart-on-switch.

## Evidence (measured trade-offs)

1. **Per-slot context (LP-0MVAZQS82004YTE9, derived):** effective WARM ceiling = 100,000 at N=1 **and** N=2 (economic ceiling `round(0.3815×262144)=100,000` binds; physical clamps 258,048 / 126,976 exceed it). Only N=3 drops to the physical clamp **83,285**, pushing the 83–100k band remote (~4.9% fast / 3.4% cheap of routing checks). **N=1→2 costs zero local-eligible context.**
2. **Contention/queue-timeout (LP-0MVAZPQUM006EAC7, two independent runs @3 concurrent):** N=1 queue-timeout **70.6–75%**; N=2 **20–25%** (12/12 completed, 0 errors each). Matches the item's historical evidence (fast 1-slot → 173 `fallback_after_queue`; cheap 3-slot → 207 over a longer window).
3. **Viability:** llama-server started cleanly at N=1 and N=2 (no OOM; ~84 GB MemAvailable). N=3 had one `--parallel` start mismatch in the invalid run (recorded, not hidden).
4. **Memory:** no OOM at any N; GPU-memory capture degraded (~0.2 GB) — reported non-available rather than hidden.

## Fidelity caveats (explicit)

- Local-slot **decode share could not be isolated live**: both sweep runs report `local share 0.0%` because concurrent audit/herdr sessions held the local dispatch lease (`local_dispatch_denied`), so benchmark requests fell back remote. TTFT/TPS therefore reflect remote fallback, not local decode — recorded in the sweep item's validity note. The **queue-timeout rates ARE valid** (measured contention under real concurrency), which is what the 1/2/3 decision hinges on.
- Full per-slot KV memory not directly measured; reported where available.

## Follow-up (AC4, created)

- **LP-0MVCGYAI80084PCZ** — Converge fast/cheap slot counts to N=2 and make the mode switch non-destructive via the llama-server adopt path (child of the parent).

## Docs / comments (AC6)

- Updated `proxy/README.md` (operating modes + slot configuration with verdict), `proxy/config.yaml` and `proxy/proxy/mode.py` comments; verdict doc under `docs/`.

RESOLVED - root cause was NOT a missing key. Session ID: herdr-1792189917-2820042-19001 - /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-llm--/2026-10-16T22-31-57-493Z_herdr-1792189917-2820042-19001.jsonl

## Root cause

My first fix attempt (adding `munitoai-free` to auth.json, per the documented name) did not work. `resolve_from_auth_json` in `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` lowercases the env var name and strips the `_api_key` suffix, then does an **exact** dict lookup with no hyphen/underscore normalisation:

- `MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY` -> `munitoai_free_api_key` -> stem `munitoai_free` (underscore)
- `munitoai-free` (hyphen, the name documented at `proxy/config.yaml:254`) therefore never matches.

So the key had to be added under `munitoai_free`, not `munitoai-free`.

## Fix applied (operator-authorised)

- `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`: added `munitoai_free` = `{type: api_key, key: <copy of munitoai.key>}` (mode 600 preserved; backup at `auth.json.bak.20261016T233626`). The `munitoai-free` alias was also left in place.
- No secret committed to the repository.

## Verification

- Resolver test: `MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY` now resolves via suffix-strip (`munitoai_free`).
- `bash proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart` completes: `[env] MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY resolved from ~/.pi/agent/auth.json`, then `=== Starting proxy server ===`.
- `curl http://localhost:8000/health` -> `status: healthy`, `ready: true`, `llama_server_running: true`, `tts_server_running: true`, `tts_server_healthy: true`, `backend_reachable: true`.
- Copied key accepted by the free-tier endpoint: `POST https://api.munito.ai/inference/v1/chat/completions` (model `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`, max_tokens=1) returned HTTP 200 with a real completion.

## AC status

- AC1 (key resolvable without committing the secret): MET.
- AC2 (start-proxy completes + healthy with llama + TTS): MET.
- AC3 (record reason; cover a resolver mis-map with a test): the resolver IS judged to mis-map the documented name, so the test is delegated to the follow-up defect item LP-0MVBJXZY5002UW10. Item left open pending that.

## Intake interview — round 1 (OPEN QUESTIONs, awaiting producer answers)

**Evidence gathered so far (no questions needed, recorded for the brief):**
- `munitoai-free` (`proxy/config-fast.yaml` lines 48–61, 104–117, and the same entries in `proxy/config.yaml`) sits immediately after `local-qwen3` in the `plan`/`author`/`code` chains and has **no** `rate_limit_rpm`, so nothing gates it.
- The proxy already has a **proactive 60-second sliding-window RPM gate**: `SlidingWindowRateLimiter.check_and_increment()` (`proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py`) invoked before dispatch in both fallback entry points (`provider.py:5900`, `provider.py:6840`). When the budget is exhausted it logs `Rate limited: skipping provider=…`, records `status=rate_limited`, and `continue`s to the next provider — i.e. **immediate pass-through, no waiting**. `rate_limit_rpm` is undocumented in any shipped config and is used by no provider today.
- `SlidingWindowRateLimiter.remaining()` exists but is never called — no capacity visibility in `/status`.
- Observed on 2026-10-18: up to 6 concurrent `MunitoAI Free` streams; `HTTP 429 rate_limit_exceeded` fallbacks; `fallback_after_queue` reasons. Upstream retries (`upstream_retry_max_attempts: 3`) do not re-consume budget.
- Neighbour items: `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L` (open, header-driven reset/cooldown — reactive), `LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N` (completed, per-account 429 must not exclude the paid sibling).

**Q1 (OPEN QUESTION) — what does the free tier's 60 s limit actually bound?** (a) request-rate budget, N requests per 60 s window; (b) concurrency, at most N in-flight streams; (c) per-request duration capped at 60 s upstream. *Agent preference: (a)* — matches the existing 60 s sliding-window gate and the observed burst pattern.

**Q2 (OPEN QUESTION) — how should the proxy learn the remaining capacity?** (a) static per-entry `rate_limit_rpm`; (b) derive from `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests` / `x-ratelimit-limit-requests` / `x-ratelimit-reset-requests` response headers (overlaps `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L`); (c) static cap now + header feedback later. *Agent preference: (c), with only the static cap in scope here.*

**Q3 (OPEN QUESTION) — acceptance bar for 'not over-using the free tier'?** (a) no upstream 429 from `munitoai-free` observed over a 24 h window; (b) every over-budget request logs `rate_limited` and proceeds to the next tier without waiting; (c) both. *Agent preference: (c).*

## Preliminary results — run on demand, 2026-10-18 14:06 (post-change window ≈ 1.05 h)

**Verdict so far: working as designed — keep `rate_limit_rpm: 10` for now; confirm with the full 12 h window at the scheduled 02:05 run.**

**Window correction:** the gate went live earlier than the manual restart I mentioned earlier — commit `b71d743a` landed on `dev` at **12:39:25**, and the api-triggered restart at **13:05:09** loaded it. Post-change window therefore = 13:05:09 → 14:06:19 (1.02 h); baseline = the 12 h ending 13:05:09. Two further restarts fell inside the window (13:25:19 mode→fast, 13:59:38 manual), which reset the in-memory window and interrupted requests.

| Metric | Baseline (12 h) | Post-change (1.02 h) |
|---|---|---|
| `munito.ai` dispatches | 2 846 (3.95/min) | 303 (4.95/min) |
| Rolling-60 s max | **72** @ 01:08 | **11** @ 13:27 |
| Per-minute p50 / p95 / max | 4 / 20 / 44 | 5 / **10** / **10** |
| Minutes at/over the 10 cap | 96 (21.9 % of active min) | 11 (19.3 % of active min) |
| Minutes with any free-tier use | 439 (61.0 % of all min) | 57 (**93.2 %** of all min) |
| Upstream `429` markers | **19** (0.67 % of dispatches) | **0** |
| `All providers exhausted` | 1 | 0 |
| MunitoAI TTFT p50 / p95 | 0.560 s / 19.85 s | 0.587 s / **11.15 s** |

**AC1 — gate holds:** yes. Per-minute dispatch max is exactly 10 and never exceeds it; the single rolling-60 s reading of 11 is edge jitter (the limiter measures at decision time, the log timestamp is the POST a few ms later, so a decision just inside one window can land just outside it).

**AC2 — new sessions pass through with no wait:** 12 `Provider budget exhausted: … reason=rate_limited session_affinity=false` skips, **no wait of any kind** (there is no `session_affinity=false` entry in the wait log), each followed by dispatch on the next tier. Exhaustion diagnostics record them as `status=rate_limited` with `limit_rpm`/`remaining`/`reason`.

**AC3 — in-progress sessions wait, bounded:** 43 `wait start`, **43 satisfied, 0 exhausted, 0 aborted** — every wait produced a free-tier dispatch, none hit the 60 s cap and none lost a client. Wait distribution: p50 **14.1 s**, p95 **52.5 s**, max **55.4 s** (total 843 s across 43 requests, mean 19.6 s). No TTFT regression on the tier (p95 actually improved).

**AC4 — upstream 429s:** 19 in the baseline 12 h → **0** in the post-change hour. This is the failure mode the item was created for: agents were previously burning the allowance into `rate_limit_exceeded`.

**AC5 — free-tier utilisation preserved:** the tier is *not* starved — it is used in 93 % of minutes (vs 61 % baseline) at p50 5 dispatches/min, and saturates the cap in 19 % of active minutes (≈ baseline's 22 %). So the budget is absorbing the burst without idling the free tier.

**AC6 — recommendation:** keep `rate_limit_rpm: 10`; keep `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds: 60` (p95 wait 52.5 s shows the cap is doing real work at the top end — do not raise it without evidence); keep `provider_affinity_ttl_seconds: 900`. Re-check at the scheduled run for: (a) whether the 19 % cap-saturation share rises (would push cost onto paid tiers), (b) whether waits stay under the cap under sustained load, (c) whether upstream 429s stay at zero.

**Caveats:** one hour of data, two in-window restarts, and a 60 s boundary jitter of ±1 dispatch. Figures above are a preliminary read; the one-shot scheduled run at 2026-10-19 02:05 re-measures the full 12 h window and will replace them.

## Preliminary read — on-demand run 2026-10-18 17:35 (post-change window ≈ 4.2 h)

**Verdict (preliminary): the budget works as designed — the 10/min gate **holds** (measured == simulated cap-10 served exactly, both windows), upstream 429s dropped to ~0.3 % of dispatches, waits stay within the 15 s cap, and free-tier utilisation is preserved. The earlier sibling item LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4 already raised `rate_limit_rpm` 10 → 15 (commit `3a686659`, live at the **17:27 restart**); the measurement below is for the 10-era and the new 15-era is flagged separately.**

**CRITICAL note for the scheduled 02:05 run:** the live config is now `rate_limit_rpm: 15` (reserve 0.3, 15 s wait) since the 17:27 restart — NOT the 10 this item was designed to evaluate. The scheduled run must split its post-change window into the **10-era (13:05:09 → 17:27:00)** and the **15-era (17:27:00 → 02:05)**, or state explicitly which era it evaluates against which budget.

### Windows (log timestamps; rotation-agnostic parser over proxy.log + rotated siblings)
| window | span | hours | munito dispatches | upstream 429s (% of disp) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base (pre-gate) | 10-18 01:05 → 13:05 | 12.0 | 2 846 | 11 (0.39 %) |
| v1 (rpm 10, wait 60 s) | 13:05:09 → 14:23:12 | 1.3 | 414 | 0 |
| v2 (rpm 10, reserve .3, wait 15 s) | 14:23:12 → 17:27 | 3.1 | 1 513 | 4 (0.26 %) |
| v3 (rpm 15, reserve .3, wait 15 s) | 17:27 → 17:31 | 0.07 | 128 (32/min) | 2 |

### AC1 — gate holds (rolling-60 s cap 10)
- Committed calibration (`proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`, limiter's own `<=`-pruned sliding window): **measured served == simulated cap-10 served exactly — v1: 414 = 414; v2: 1 513 = 1 513.** The limiter enforces 10 dispatches/rolling-60 s.
- Calendar-minute bucket max 20 (15:24) / rolling readings up to 23 at 17:24:18 are **not** cap violations: the limiter measures at decision time while the log timestamp is the POST a few ms later (rolling-window straddle), and **in-flight retries of the same logical request re-log "Stream started" without a new budget slot** (e.g. 17:24 minute: 15 POST lines from only 7 distinct `x-client-request-id`s). Dispatch-rate distribution (free, by minute): p50 **10**, p95 **10**, max 20 — i.e. the gate holds at exactly the cap.

### AC2 — new-session skips never wait
- v2 skips: **946** `Provider budget exhausted: skipping … session_affinity=false`, **0** with `session_affinity=true`.
- Wait-start events with `session_affinity=false`: **0** (of 930). Confirmed at the code level — the wait path is only entered for sessions with recorded affinity (`provider.py` → `acquire_provider_budget`).

### AC3 — in-progress waits, bounded ≤ 15 s
- v2: 930 wait start, **603 satisfied / 324 exhausted / 1 aborted / 0 declined**.
- Wait durations (satisfied+exhausted+aborted, n=928): p50 **7.9 s**, p95 **15.0 s**, max **15.0 s**, **0 > 15 s** ✓ (exhausted waits sit at exactly the 15 s cap, as designed).
- No TTFT regression on the tier (see latency below).

### AC4 — upstream 429s massively reduced
- 11 → 0 → 4: base 0.39 % of munito dispatches → v1 0 % → v2 0.26 % (4 in 3.1 h). Failure mode the item was created for (agents burning the allowance into `rate_limit_exceeded`) is eliminated.
- 429 onset knee (pre-gate): rolling-60 s dispatch rate at a 429 was min 8 / median 27 / max 63; per-minute 429 rate climbs from ~4 % (10–14/min) to 19.8 % (20–29/min) — the knee is ≈ 20/min, which is what justified raising to 15 (low-risk band).

### AC5 — free-tier utilisation preserved
- v1: used in 92.3 % of minutes, p50 5 disp/min. v2: used in **100 %** of minutes, p50 9 disp/min, 8.2 disp/active-min — not starved, but **v2 demand (rolling arrivals) p50 14 / p95 32 / max 47, share of minutes > 10 = 67.9 %** → at peak the cap is saturated and ~45 % of arrivals spill (93 % of spills → `opencode-go-3`; measured paid share 46 % at peak). The tier is right-sized at 10 for calm periods and under-provisioned at afternoon peaks (arithmetically unavoidable spill).

### AC6 — regression check
- `All providers exhausted`: base 1 → v1 0 → v2 0. No terminal 503 rise.
- MunitoAI TTFT: base p90 13.7 / p95 28.0 / p99 72.9 → v2 9.6 / 21.1 / 55.2 (no rise; waits are bounded so latency did not degrade).

### Recommendation (preliminary)
- **`rate_limit_rpm: 10` was effective for its purpose** (gate holds, 429s ~eliminated, waits ≤ 15 s, free tier utilised). It is **under-provisioned at afternoon demand peaks** (demand p50 14/min ≫ 10) → that spill is a config trade-off, not a failure.
- Raising to **15** (already applied by LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4, live 17:27) sits below the ≈20/min 429 knee and cuts peak spill ~40 % (45 % → 28 %); early 15-era data shows demand 32/min with 2 upstream 429s in the first 4 min — consistent with "sporadic, not sustained"; the rollback trigger in LP-0MVE0LUXN004PCO0 covers regression.
- **Keep** `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds: 15` (cap verified to hold, 0 waits > 15 s; the 60 s era's p95 waits were the earlier latency problem) and **keep** `provider_affinity_ttl_seconds: 900`.
- Longer term the static value should give way to header-derived budgeting (`LP-0MVDNP36J006430L`) once the 15-era has a full window.
- No config/code change performed in this read-only session (per constraints).

### Caveats
- v2 spans 3.1 h only; in-window restarts at 13:25/13:59 (pre-v2). Scheduled 02:05 run replaces these with the full 12 h window; reproduce with the committed script:

**Reserve (AC1/AC2).** `provider_budget.reserved_slots(rpm, config)` = `min(floor(rpm * provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio), rpm - 1)`, 0 when `rpm <= 1` or the ratio is 0. `acquire_provider_budget()` now applies a per-request cap: in-progress sessions (affinity) use the full `rate_limit_rpm`; new/anonymous sessions use `new_session_limit()` = `rpm - reserve` (7 of 10 with the shipped values). data.comment:
### Answering 'is the rate limit used for any other provider?' (fact-finding for this item)

Resolved config across both modes — `rate_limit_rpm` is declared on **exactly one logical entry**:

| Entry | Type | Endpoint | `rate_limit_rpm` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `munitoai-free` (plan/author/code) | remote | api.munito.ai | **10** |
| `munitoai` (paid) | remote | api.munito.ai | — |
| `opencode-go-3` / `-2` / `-go` | remote | opencode.ai/zen/go | — |
| `opencode-go-compact` | remote | opencode.ai/zen/go | — |
| `deepseek-flash` / `-compact` | remote | api.deepseek.com | — |
| `github-primary` | remote | models.inference.ai.azure.com | — |
| `local-qwen3` / `local-embed` | local | — | — |

So the capability is **dormant for every other provider** (it was already before the free-tier work: no shipped config ever set it). Any paid tier could opt in later — e.g. to protect a per-key concurrency/rate ceiling on `opencode` or a paid MunitoAI plan — which is exactly why per-model + per-entry controls matter: today the *behaviour* knobs (reserve ratio, wait cap, waiter depth, affinity TTL) are global, so opting a second provider in would force all chains to share one tuning.

Note for implementers: the budget bucket is keyed by provider **entry name**, so `plan`/`author`/`code` share one 10/min window. Per-model knobs change *how* a model behaves against that shared window, not the size of the window.

## Appendix: planning questions & decisions

Recorded by the `plan` skill session `herdr-1792390902-3844878-15177`.

### Q1. Which opencode-go entry joins the low chain?
`proxy/config.yaml` defines three equivalent entries: `opencode-go-3` (OPENCODE_3_API_KEY), `opencode-go-2` (OPENCODE_2_API_KEY), `opencode-go` (OPENCODE_API_KEY), all with `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and identical `available_times`.
**Answer (eng, recommended, for confirmation):** `opencode-go-3` — it is first in the medium/high provider lists for the code model, so reusing it for the low chain keeps prompt-cache affinity aligned with the hot path. Evidence: `proxy/config.yaml` model `code` → `providers[2].name == opencode-go-3`.
**Status:** OPEN QUESTION (confirm at implementation).

### Q2. UTC vs local window alignment
`available_times` are **UTC**; the priority cheap window (`priority_window: 01:00–10:00`) is **local time**.
**Research:** host timezone is `Europe/Dublin` (IST, +0100 in October), so the cheap window is UTC **00:00–09:00**. opencode-go windows are UTC `["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`, i.e. unavailable UTC `01:00–04:00` and `06:00–10:00`. Overlap = UTC `00:00–01:00` + `04:00–06:00` = **3 of 9 cheap hours**. Evidence: `date -u` output and `proxy/config.yaml` `available_times` / `priority_window`.
**Answer (recommended):** keep `available_times` unchanged — "off-peak only" is the requirement, and the gaps are deliberate paid-spend avoidance. Document the 3-of-9 overlap in config comments so the limitation is explicit rather than surprising.
**Status:** decided for this item; the widening question is an OPEN QUESTION below.

### OPEN QUESTION (operator): widen the windows?
The change yields ~3 extra hours of local-overflow capacity per night, not 9. If more cheap-window coverage is wanted, opencode-go `available_times` would need to cover UTC `01:00–04:00` and `06:00–10:00` too — which means paid spend in the currently-excluded hours. This item deliberately does **not** do that. Directed to the operator; matters because it is the difference between a 3-hour and a 9-hour fix.

### Q3. Should the `compact` model's low chain change?
`compact` already chains `low: [opencode-go-compact, deepseek-flash-compact]` — it has no local tier and already leads with opencode-go.
**Answer (eng):** no. Out of scope; leave untouched.

### Duplicate-work check
`wl search "opencode-go"` / `"off-peak"` / `"low priority"` reviewed. Nearest neighbours: LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P (added the off-peak `available_times` windows — prerequisite, completed), LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA (introduced priority routing and the `low = local + free` chain — the constraint being relaxed here, completed), LP-0MSMIPPJI007GU9N (cheap mode keeps remote enabled — completed). **No duplicate found:** none adds opencode-go to a `low` chain.

## Operator decision recorded — plan revised

**Q1 resolved:** do **not** pick a single opencode entry — add **all** opencode models to the low chain, gated by their existing `available_times`.

**Q2 resolved:** do **not** widen `available_times`. The off-peak windows stay exactly as they are; paid spend remains confined to them. The measured 3-of-9-hour overlap is therefore accepted as the intended benefit, not a defect to fix.

Resulting target chain for plan/author/code:

`local-qwen3 → munitoai-free → opencode-go-3 → opencode-go-2 → opencode-go`

### Why "all three" is substantive, not cosmetic (new evidence)

Rate-limit quarantine is keyed on the **API-key account**, not the gateway:
`_usage_limit_account_key()` = `api_key_env@endpoint` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:4075-4090`, LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW / LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N). A 429 on `opencode-go-3` poisons only that account, so `opencode-go-2` and `opencode-go` are still tried in the same request with independent quota → genuine 3× rate-limit capacity. This is exactly the failure mode observed (16 upstream 429s from `api.munito.ai`, `rate_limited` 1540).

**Caveat recorded (added as an AC and a required doc point):** for 5xx/stall failures the same-gateway siblings ARE skipped as one failure domain (`_failure_domain_key` / `attempted_domains`, LP-0MSG45I8Q0020N1F), so the three entries do **not** multiply capacity during an opencode outage. Expected, but must be documented to avoid a false resilience assumption.

### Correction to the earlier problem statement

The parent description previously said `munitoai-free` was capped at `rate_limit_rpm: 15`. That figure came from the config's documentation comment; the **actual** per-model values are `rate_limit_rpm: 2` for plan/author/code. Corrected in the description — it makes the overflow problem materially worse than first stated (2 req/min, and it is the last entry in the chain).

### Revision log

- Parent LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX: ACs rewritten (all-three ordering, windows-unchanged proof, per-key-429 and same-domain-5xx tests, no paid-tier leak).
- Test item LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1: added per-key-429 failover + same-domain-5xx assertions; fixed test-invocation convention to `/skill:test`.
- Impl item LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I: chain widened to all three entries; "zero changed `available_times` lines" added as an AC.
- Verify item LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO: added per-key dispatch counting and a zero-leak check for the gap windows.
